note: Sortable Views adds drag-and-drop ordering to Views; new order is written into an integer entity field via AJAX (route sortableviews.ajax -> AjaxController::ajaxSave). It provides three Views style plugins (sortable_default, sortable_html_list, sortable_table), each with a weight_field option; a field handler sortable_views_handle (drag handle) and an area handler save_sortable_changes (save button), added to every entity base table via hook_views_data_alter. No settings page, permissions (uses core entity update access), or Drush. Medium cases inspect a real View config (its sortable style + weight_field); hard cases switch a view to a sortable style with a weight_field, and add the drag-handle field + save area, verified against live view config.

evals.prompt: Which Views display formats (style plugins) does the sortableviews module provide, and what style option tells it where to store the drag-and-drop order?
evals.expected_output: Three style plugins: sortable_default (unformatted list), sortable_html_list, and sortable_table. Each exposes a 'weight_field' option naming the view field (mapping to an integer entity field) where the order is stored.

evals.prompt: To make a View sortable with sortableviews, which two extra handlers must I add to the view (one to drag, one to save), and what are they called?
evals.expected_output: Add the field 'Sortableviews: Drag and drop handle.' (id sortable_views_handle) for the drag grip, and the header/footer area 'Save Sortableviews changes' (id save_sortable_changes) for the save button. Also set the sortable style's weight_field and add that field as a sort criterion.

evals.prompt: Where does sortableviews store the sort order, and how does that differ from Draggable Views?
evals.expected_output: It writes the new order directly into an integer field on each entity (via the Field API / weight_field), saving each entity. Draggable Views instead keeps weights in its own dedicated table. Authorization reuses core entity 'update' access.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a View named 'sortableviews_demo' that is set up for drag-and-drop ordering. Inspect the live view configuration and state which sortableviews style (format) its default display uses.
evals.expected_output: The sortableviews_demo view's default display uses the sortable_table style.

evals.prompt: On this site, the 'sortableviews_demo' View saves its drag-and-drop order into a field. Inspect the live view configuration and give the machine name of the weight field configured in its sortable style.
evals.expected_output: The sortable style's weight_field option on sortableviews_demo is field_sv_weight.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a View 'sortableviews_task' whose default display uses the plain core unformatted-list format. Using sortableviews, change its default display's format to a Sortable Views style and set the style's weight field to field_sv_weight. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set the default display's style type to a sortable style (sortable_default / sortable_html_list / sortable_table) with options.weight_field = 'field_sv_weight' and save the view.

evals.prompt: On this site the View 'sortableviews_ha' already uses a Sortable Views style with a weight field, but users cannot yet drag or save. Add the sortableviews drag-and-drop handle field and the 'Save Sortableviews changes' area to its default display, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add a field with plugin_id sortable_views_handle to the display's fields, and an area with plugin_id save_sortable_changes to the header or footer, then save the view.
